analysis.title: GS Blekos - Marketcolour + Nvidia / Whitbread / Prysmian / Banks 18 Nov 2026
key_insights: US equities fell for a second leg: SPX -103bps to 7340 with all 11 sectors lower, VIX above 25, and the S&P 500 closing below its 200-day moving average for the first time since April. NDX fell 72bps to 27001 and RTY fell 150bps to 2701.
Financials (-1.87%) and Utilities (-1.60%) were the weakest US sectors. The GS High Beta Momentum basket (+1.92%) and GS Momentum Hi/Lo basket (+1.67%) outperformed.
European equities had their worst day since March: SXXP -1.8% with 92% of stocks closing lower. EU Semis (-2.9%) and Software (-4.4%) led the decline.

Nvidia said token prices have fallen nearly 60% since May, which is raising token usage and compute demand. GPU rental prices are rising across generations: Hopper GPUs re-contracted at up to 2x their original price, and B300 rates are up more than 60% since launch.

Nvidia (GS Buy, PT $220, 40% upside, 8.6x 2028 P/E) reported revenue of $115.8bn vs consensus $109.5bn, gross margin of 74.9% vs 73.5%, and Data Center revenue of $107.6bn vs $102.0bn. Management raised its CY27 revenue growth forecast to +75% from +70%. Rubin generated $20bn of revenue in its first quarter. Financial commitments to customers and supply chain partners stand at $518bn.

Nike's investor day was not enough for GS. Management sees FY29 as the turning point and still expects sales to fall by a high-single-digit percentage in FY2027 as it cuts Sportswear and Jordan supply and resets China.

Whitbread (GS rating 'Up to B', PT GBP37, 32% upside): GS sees PBT growing at a 14% CAGR over FY27-31E and ROCE expanding by about 680bps by FY31E vs FY27E. Buybacks could begin next year. The shares trade near their 10+ year trough multiple.

Prysmian (GS Buy, PT EUR174, 60% upside): GS raised FY26-28E adj. EBITDA by about 2-3% after the 3Q26 beat. GS expects 2026 EBITDA above the top of guidance and 2027 adj. EBITDA guidance above EUR4bn at full-year results.

Eurobank announced a purchase of 65% of Bulgarian bank Fibank. The deal is worth EUR1bn for 100%, funded by excess capital plus a EUR750m ABB (4% of market cap). GS sees 7% EPS accretion, 12% PAT accretion pro forma for the share capital increase, and a 21% return on consumed capital pro forma for cost synergies.

BNP's BNL deep dive set new 2030 targets: revenue growth above 3% (consensus 2.4%), NII growth of 2.5%, fee growth of 4%, cost/income of 56% (consensus 57%), and RWA falling 0.5% a year (consensus rising).

Smiths Group 1Q organic revenue growth was 0%, light vs whispers of about 3%. The company kept its FY guide of about 4% and expects acceleration through the year, with John Crane weighted to H2 and Flex-Tek to H1, after Middle East disruption hit John Crane early in the year.

market_movers.rationale: Revenue, gross margin and Data Center revenue all beat consensus, and management raised its CY27 growth forecast to +75%. GS cites 40% upside and 8.6x 2028 P/E against neutral-to-negative investor positioning.
GS raised FY26-28E adj. EBITDA by about 2-3% after the 3Q26 beat and sees 2026 EBITDA above the top of guidance. Prysmian (no US listing) has 60% upside to the target.
GS sees earnings, returns on capital and shareholder returns improving sooner than the market expects, while Whitbread trades near its 10+ year trough multiple. Upside to target is 32%.
